 Article content Toronto has struggled against good opponents in recent seasons, but the ineptness has risen to peak levels when Jalen Brunson, Karl-Anthony Towns and Co. have been the opposition.
 New York has won the last 13 meetings, including five times in 2025-26. It’s been nearly four full years since the Raptors prevailed and in that span the franchises, who have a history of significant trades with each other dating back to Toronto dealing for Doug Christie and later swapping Marcus Camby for Charles Oakley in the late-1990s, pulled off another blockbuster. OG Anunoby went to New York (with Precious Achiuwa, who has found new NBA life in Sacramento but never did much with the Knicks), for RJ Barrett and Immanuel Quickley. Anunoby was a popular Raptor, but has become a cult icon amongst Knicks fans thanks to his exploits last spring, including one of the most memorable tip-ins in NBA history .

 Article content Advertisement 3 Story continues below This advertisement has not loaded yet, but your article continues below. Article content Why the Knicks have Toronto’s number
 With the Knicks in town for a two-game mini series Sunday and Tuesday it’s worth examining some reasons why they’ve dominated the matchup.
 The first area is size. Part of the reason why the Knicks won it all last year and probably should have made it to the NBA Final the year before has a lot to do with the fact they are bigger and stronger overall than most opponents, capable of out-rebounding them on most nights and aggressively defending anyone. They also have tended to generate a ton of offensive rebounds and have great team chemistry, partly owing to so much of the core playing collegiately together while at Villanova.
 Toronto, with the burly Anunoby now playing for the other side and Pascal Siakam (who scored 52 points in one of Toronto’s most recent wins over the Knicks) also dealt away, hasn’t had the length and athleticism up front to compete most nights with Anunoby, Karl-Anthony Towns (and Julius Randle before that), Mitchell Robinson and even the tenacious Josh Hart (who is basically a far better version of former Raptors and Knicks forward Jerome Williams). Kawhi Leonard would change things, but he will miss these games.
 Advertisement 4 Story continues below This advertisement has not loaded yet, but your article continues below. Article content Scottie Barnes also makes a difference, but he’s banged up and might not be available either. Without both it’s hard to see Jakob Poeltl, Collin Murray-Boyles and Allen Graves being able to overcome New York’s size, length, strength and skill advantages up front. Toronto has only won the rebounding battle twice over the last 13 meetings and there have been a few times the Knicks grabbed close to 50% more rebounds. The Knicks again lead all in rebounding though it’s interesting that Toronto is second in offensive rebound percentage. Robinson might be gone to rival Boston, but Towns is still there and he’s only averaged 21.5 points and 13.5 rebounds while shooting 52% over his last 10 games against Toronto.
 Toronto’s also had issues slowing Knicks star point guard Jalen Brunson. He’s shot nearly 50% from the field against them too over the last three years and better than that in the five wins last season.
 When the streak was first starting Toronto was in the midst of a rebuild which partly explains the poor results. More recently though they should have been able to pull out a win or two.
 Advertisement 5 Story continues below This advertisement has not loaded yet, but your article continues below. Article content When will the streak end?
 The teams will meet again twice early in 2027, hopefully for Toronto’s sake with both Leonard and Barnes in the lineup. But there’s a chance the losing skid can end either Sunday or Tuesday. The Knicks aren’t exactly firing on all cylinders coming in, with a .500 record and perhaps a championship hangover slowing them 12 games in. The teams are tied for 11th in the league in offensive efficiency, though the Knicks rank fifth defensively to Toronto’s distant 15th.
 Barnes went through part of practice Saturday and hates to miss time (he’s already been out four games after only two absences all of last season), but it’s a long season and rushing doesn’t make sense for anyone.
